## Extra for exercise 15
Ektra for exercise 15 from the book
In exercise 15 you compared three alleles and found denovo mutations. 
Spotting a de novo mutation would not be that easy in a real life, as it was in the small sequences you just compared, as the genome is much much longer than that. Imagine having to comapare thousands ands thousands of basepairs in the same way as you did in exercise 15 - that would be tiresome really fast!

Thankfully we have different tools that can help with this today. Try and run the code piece below and take a look at the sequences. Then run the next code piece and look at where the code found de novo mutations.

The code below uploads a csv file containing sequences for a part of the alleles from two parents and their child.

```{python}
seq = load_dataset('seq_data')
# Display the full string instead of truncating it
display(HTML(
    seq.to_html(index=False, escape=True)
))
```

Now we can use the codepiece below to highlight the differences in the childs allel sequences that not found in either the mother or fathers alleles.(You dont have to understand the code. Just see that very few lines can save us from a lot of manual labour.)

```{python}
def de_novo_mut(mom1, mom2, dad1, dad2, child, show_html=True, line_length=100):
    highlighted = []
    mutation_positions = []
    
    for i in range(len(child)):
        if child[i] in [mom1[i], mom2[i], dad1[i], dad2[i]]:
            highlighted.append(child[i])
        else:
            highlighted.append(f'<span style="color: red; font-weight: bold;">{child[i]}</span>')
            mutation_positions.append(i + 1)

    if show_html:
        html_lines = []
        for start in range(0, len(highlighted), line_length):
            line = ''.join(highlighted[start:start+line_length])
            html_lines.append(line)
        html_code = '<div style="white-space: pre; font-family: monospace; line-height: 1.5em; border: 1px solid #ddd; padding: 10px; text-align: left;">'
        html_code += '<br>'.join(html_lines)
        html_code += '</div>'
        display(HTML(html_code))
    
    return mutation_positions

```

The last codepiece prints the sequences and hightligts the found de novo mutations

```{python}
# --- Run mutation detection and show results ---
print("Analyzing Child allele 1:")
mutations_found_1 = de_novo_mut(seq['Sequence'][0], seq['Sequence'][1], seq['Sequence'][2], seq['Sequence'][3], seq['Sequence'][4])
print(f"Found {len(mutations_found_1)} de novo mutations at positions: {mutations_found_1}\n")

print("Analyzing Child allele 2:")
mutations_found_2 =de_novo_mut(seq['Sequence'][0], seq['Sequence'][1], seq['Sequence'][2], seq['Sequence'][3], seq['Sequence'][5])
print(f"Found {len(mutations_found_2)} de novo mutations at positions: {mutations_found_2}")
```
